title: The Pinterest Strategy That's Actually Working for Me in 2026
key_points: Pinterest is a search engine, not social media — it works more closely to Google than Instagram
People on Pinterest are already looking for info and inspiration and are open to purchasing
Create a new business Pinterest account separate from personal accounts for organization, customer experience, and SEO purposes
Use Pinterest Trends feature by clicking the search icon in the top right to type in keywords and see what people are searching for
Pinterest Trends shows data on when things trend at specific times of year through visible dips in the graphs
When creating a pin, you must provide: photo, title, description, link, and tags — all opportunities to use researched keywords
Search your product keywords on Pinterest to see what types of photos are ranking in popular pins and take note of aesthetics
Use ChatGPT by pasting your keywords and asking for an SEO-driven Pinterest title and description to copy directly into pins
Create 3 pins per product with different photos, different SEO, and different hashtags in descriptions
Post one pin per product per week across three weeks — not three pins of the same product on consecutive days
For 5 products, you should have 15 photos total creating 15 pins
Pinterest is a longer-term strategy — expect to start getting readable impressions in your first 1-2 months
Pins from years ago still bring traffic because Pinterest doesn't deprioritize older content like social media does
Using Pinterest Trends keywords may result in quicker increases in impressions and clicks
For Shopify, link pins to the checkout page instead of the product page so customers can immediately purchase using Apple Pay or PayPal
For Etsy, link pins directly to the specific product listing, not your whole Etsy shop
Linking to Etsy shop instead of products results in favorites but not conversions; direct product links get items into customer carts
Items in Etsy carts appear when customers return to Etsy, bringing them back to your product
summary:
The video opens by stating that many Etsy sellers use Pinterest incorrectly by randomly posting pins without strategy. Pinterest is positioned as a search engine similar to Google rather than social media like Instagram, meaning users are actively searching for information and inspiration and are open to purchasing. The strategy works for any platform — Etsy, Shopify, or TikTok shop — because Pinterest allows links to be added to pins.

The first step recommended is creating a new business Pinterest account separate from any personal account. This keeps everything organized for both customer experience (people do look at Pinterest boards) and SEO purposes, rather than mixing business content with personal saved items like clothes and food ideas.

For research, the video highlights Pinterest Trends as a hidden feature many people don't know about. By clicking the search icon in the top right of Pinterest Trends and typing in keywords, sellers can see what people are searching for and when items trend at specific times of year. This keyword research should inform the title, description, and tags when creating pins. Additionally, searching keywords on Pinterest shows what types of photos are ranking in popular pins, providing guidance on aesthetics. For writing pin copy, the video suggests pasting keywords into ChatGPT and asking for an SEO-driven Pinterest title and description.

The posting strategy involves creating 3 pins per product, each with different photos, different SEO text, and different hashtags. These are scheduled one per week across three weeks rather than posting all three consecutively. For example, with 5 products, you would create 15 total pins. Week one posts one variation of each of the 5 products, week two posts a second variation of each, and week three posts the third variation. This keeps the Pinterest page aesthetic and avoids overloading the algorithm with repeated identical products.

Regarding results, Pinterest is described as a longer-term strategy where readable impressions should be expected within the first 1-2 months. Unlike social media where content fails if it doesn't perform in the first 20 minutes, Pinterest categorizes content by keywords and continues showing it long-term — pins from years ago still generate traffic. Using Pinterest Trends keywords may accelerate impression growth.

For conversions, the video recommends specific linking strategies: Shopify sellers should link to the checkout page rather than the product page so customers can immediately pay via Apple Pay or PayPal. Etsy sellers cannot link to checkout but should link directly to the specific product listing rather than the whole shop. The speaker shares that early on they linked to their Etsy shop and got favorites but not conversions, whereas direct product links get items into customer carts where they remain visible when customers return to Etsy.
